how: A 1992 US survey asked adults who had used drugs at least 12 times. About 1 in 3 who started at 13 or younger had been dependent on drugs. For those who started at 21 or older, it was about 1 in 7.

In New Zealand, children were asked about drinking and drugs at 13 and 15, not years later. At 32, 29 in 100 of those who used several times by 15, mostly alcohol, were dependent on alcohol or drugs. For teens with similar childhoods who had not, it was 15 in 100.
In Australian twins, the twin who started cannabis before 17 more often had drug problems by the study's rules. It was about 48 in 100, against 33 in 100 for the other twin.
A bigger twin study found the link was not strong, and much of it ran in families. Its authors think waiting longer to start would cut the risk only a little.

cards.statement: Studies show that starting to drink or use drugs young is what causes drug or drinking problems later.
People who started using drugs at 13 or younger more often became dependent than later starters.

questions: Is clonidine as good as slowly cutting down methadone for coming off opioids?

lines.short: No clear difference in how many people finished, but clonidine-type medicines caused more low blood pressure and other side effects.
lines.but: The trials were small and some were badly run, so the answer could change.
how: Twelve trials compared clonidine-type medicines with methadone given in slowly shrinking amounts.
Withdrawal felt about as bad overall, but it started and ended sooner with clonidine-type medicines.
Low blood pressure and other side effects were about twice as common as with methadone.
Neither way seemed to take away all the aches, bad sleep and worry.

cards.statement: Slowly cutting down methadone took away all the aches, bad sleep and worry of withdrawal.

questions: Is buprenorphine better than slowly cutting down methadone for coming off opioids?

lines.short: They worked about the same: similar numbers of people finished withdrawal treatment with each.
lines.but: Only six small trials, mostly in hospitals or a prison.
how: Six trials compared buprenorphine with methadone given in slowly shrinking amounts.
About 55 in 100 finished on buprenorphine and about 53 in 100 on methadone.
The trials could not show whether withdrawal felt different with one or the other.

cards.statement: Buprenorphine helped far more people finish withdrawal treatment than slowly cutting down methadone.

questions: Will I sleep badly when I stop heroin or other opioids?

lines.short: Studies in one review found shorter, lighter sleep in the first weeks after stopping heroin than in good sleepers.
lines.but: This comes second-hand from a review that did not check how good the studies were.
how: Sleep labs recorded people in their first weeks off heroin and compared them with good sleepers.
They slept less, slept more lightly, and took longer to fall asleep.
Many people on methadone also sleep badly, and long-term opioid use is linked with pauses in breathing during sleep.

cards.statement: Long-term opioid use is linked with pauses in breathing during sleep.

questions: Is it dangerous to take loperamide (Imodium) to get through opioid withdrawal?

lines.short: It can be: some people who took very large amounts got serious heart-rhythm problems.
lines.but: These were only people seen by poisons doctors, who tend to see the sicker cases, and there was no group to compare with, so the study cannot show how often this happens.
how: Doctors who treat poisonings in the USA described 26 people seen after taking loperamide; 20 of them had symptoms.
Some took it to stop withdrawal, some to feel good, and a few were young children who swallowed it by accident.
About 4 in 10 had a change on their heart tracing that can lead to a dangerous heartbeat; some needed a breathing tube or a pacemaker, and no deaths were reported.
Where the amount was recorded, the people with these heart problems had taken far more than the packet says.

cards.statement: Some people who took very large amounts of loperamide (Imodium) got serious heart-rhythm problems.

questions: Why do some people on methadone feel withdrawal before their next dose?

lines.short: In one small study, their methadone level tended to drop faster after its daily high point.
lines.but: Only 18 people were tested for one day, and by our check the difference fell just short of statistical significance, even after the authors left two people out.
how: Nine people who felt withdrawal before their next dose were compared with nine who did not.
Just before the dose, both groups had about the same level of methadone in their blood.
On average, in both groups, withdrawal was lowest in the hours after the dose and grew as the level fell.
The study did not test any change to treatment.

questions: Is it dangerous to stop methadone or buprenorphine (Suboxone)?

lines.short: Deaths were more common off treatment, most of all in the first 4 weeks after leaving. In 16 methadone studies, about 36 in 1,000 died a year off treatment, against 11 on it.
lines.but: These studies counted everyone who left, for any reason. People who leave differ in other ways, so the studies can't show that stopping itself caused the deaths.
how: In 16 groups of people on methadone, about 11 in 1,000 died each year in treatment, against about 36 out of it. Every group had more deaths out of treatment.
In the biggest recent groups the gap was smaller: about 6 or 7 deaths a year per 1,000 people in treatment, against 12 to 18 out of it.

5 recent studies, with lower death rates overall, split deaths by time: about 32 a year per 1,000 people in the first 4 weeks off methadone, against about 14 later on. The first 4 weeks on it looked riskier too, but that could be chance.

With buprenorphine (almost all the deaths in Australian studies), deaths were also higher in the first 4 weeks off, about 32 against 11 a year per 1,000, but from just two studies, so it's less certain. Counting overdoses alone, 3 methadone studies found no clear rise in those weeks, but only 20 happened then.

cards.statement: Death rates were about the same in and out of methadone treatment.
In studies, death rates were highest in the first weeks after leaving methadone.

questions: Can opioid withdrawal itself kill you?

lines.short: Deaths have been reported, but nobody knows how often. One editorial lists 11, all in jail. It suggests vomiting and diarrhoea, left untreated, can dry the body out until the heart fails.
lines.but: It's one editorial's list, built from news reports and a court case. With no count of how many people went through withdrawal, there's no rate.
how: The authors' idea: vomiting and diarrhoea that don't stop, left untreated, dry the body out. Blood sodium rises, and the heart can fail.
The cases: a woman in custody in the UK in 1998, and 10 people in US jails reported in the press from 2013 to 2016, aged 18 to 49.
The authors say each death came slowly, with time to treat it, and call the deaths neglect or a lack of medical care.
They say such deaths are rising but give no counts over time. Nothing here covers withdrawal outside custody.

cards.statement: You can't die from opioid withdrawal.

questions: Do nicotine patches and gum help people stop smoking?

lines.short: Nicotine patches, gum and similar help people who want to stop smoking.
lines.but: The gain is modest, and many trials were paid for by drug companies.
how: After 6 months or more, about 16 in 100 had stopped with nicotine replacement, against about 10 or 11 in 100 without.
The gain was bigger with a lot of support (about 8 more in 100) than with little (about 2 more).
Each form, from patches to sprays, did better than its own comparison.
These were people trying to stop, so the trials say nothing about anyone else.

questions: How does GHB affect driving?

lines.short: Soon after GHB, people crashed far more in a driving test than after a dummy drink.
lines.but: Only 16 people who had rarely or never used GHB, one dose, no alcohol, in a lab driving machine.
how: 16 healthy adults used a lab driving machine after GHB on one day and after a dummy drink on another.
On the first drive after GHB, every one of them crashed more than after the dummy drink.
Later drives that day were not clearly worse than after the dummy drink, but this small study cannot show when driving is safe again.
Four people threw up after GHB and could not finish the first drive after it, so they were left out.

cards.statement: In a lab driving test soon after GHB, every person who finished crashed more than after a dummy drink.

questions: Can a benzodiazepine sleeping pill affect my driving the next day?

lines.short: Some benzodiazepine sleeping pills made people drive worse the next day than after dummy pills.
lines.but: Most studies tested one night in healthy volunteers, not people who take these pills for months.
how: Volunteers drove a real car or a driving machine the day after a pill or a dummy pill.
Researchers measured how much the car weaved inside its lane.
With some pills the weaving was worse than with alcohol at the driving limit used in several countries.
With other pills or lower doses, weaving was not clearly different from dummy pills, but each result came from one small study.

cards.statement: A benzodiazepine sleeping pill at bedtime can't affect your driving the next day.
The day after some benzo sleeping pills, people drove worse than with alcohol at a common drink-driving limit.

questions: How long does cannabis affect your driving skills?

lines.short: For several hours; probably longer after eating it than smoking it, and longer after bigger doses.
lines.but: These are averages from lab studies, not a safe time to drive for you.
how: Researchers pooled 80 studies in which people took THC or a dummy (placebo), then did driving and attention tests.
Soon after THC, people weaved more in their lane and reacted more slowly than after the dummy.
The effects faded over several hours, probably more slowly when THC was eaten than when it was smoked or vaped.
People who use cannabis weekly or more were less affected than people who use it less often, but the study could not work out for how long.

cards.statement: Soon after THC, the main active part of cannabis, people did just as well on lab driving tests as after a dummy.

questions: How many deaths does alcohol cause worldwide?

lines.short: Global models estimated alcohol caused about 2.3 to 2.8 million deaths a year, compared with no one drinking.
lines.but: These are computer estimates built on studies of groups of people, not counted deaths.
how: The Global Burden of Disease study estimated 2.8 million deaths in 2016: about 7 in 100 deaths of men and 2 in 100 of women.
At ages 15 to 49, alcohol was the top risk factor in that study: about 12 in 100 deaths of men and 4 in 100 of women.
An older model using WHO data estimated about 2.5 million deaths caused in 2004, mostly from injuries, heart disease, cancer and cirrhosis, minus about 0.2 million it counted as prevented.
A later round of the global study, quoted second-hand, put it at about 1.8 million in 2020. The numbers move with the method, so they do not show a trend.

cards.statement: Worldwide, alcohol is estimated to cause millions of deaths a year.
In a global study, alcohol was the top risk factor for death among people aged 15 to 49.

questions: Can drugs be ranked by how much harm they do?

lines.short: Experts have tried: a UK panel ranked alcohol most harmful overall, mostly for harm to other people. For the person using, crack, heroin and meth scored worst.
lines.but: The scores are one panel's views, not measures, and alcohol's top score partly reflects how many people drink.
how: In 2010, experts scored 20 drugs on 16 harms in one day. A 2007 expert ranking put legal alcohol and tobacco above LSD and ecstasy.
Alcohol scored 72 of 100, 46 of them for harm to others. Critics say one score mixes harm per person with how many people use.
Tobacco scored zero for deaths like overdose. Lung cancer was counted elsewhere. The authors agreed it probably kills more than the other 19 drugs combined.
In an online survey, 1,501 people rated drug harms much like experts did. Of the 603 allowed to rate heroin, 467 had never used it.

cards.statement: UK experts judged legal alcohol and tobacco less harmful than LSD and ecstasy.
In a UK expert ranking, alcohol came top mostly because of the harm it does to other people.
In a UK expert ranking, alcohol scored worse than heroin or crack for the person using it.
In a UK expert ranking of 20 drugs, tobacco scored zero for deaths like overdose.

questions: Why do people use kratom, and what do they say it does?

lines.short: Mostly for pain, anxiety or depression, people told two surveys, and most felt it helped. In one, about 4 in 10 had used kratom to cut down or stop opioids.
lines.but: Both surveys reached people mostly through a pro-kratom group, and those who quit after bad experiences were left out of one and may be too few in the other.
how: In 2016 and 2017, online surveys asked 8,049 and 2,798 US adults who used kratom. Most were White, working and middle-aged.
Pain was the top reason (68 and 91 in 100), then anxiety or depression. In 2017, kratom's 'good effects' scored 86 of 100, 'high' 12.
In 2017, 1,144 had used kratom to cut down or stop opioids; 849 credited it with 6 months or more off opioids. Nobody checked.
703 felt unwell after 12 to 48 hours without kratom (2016). On a checklist, 68 of 2,798 had moderate or severe kratom use disorder (2017).

cards.statement: In a 2017 kratom survey, about 4 in 10 people said they had used kratom to cut down or stop opioids.

questions: How often is kratom found in overdose deaths?

lines.short: Kratom turned up in about 6 of every 1,000 overdose deaths in 27 US states in 2016–17. It was almost always found with other drugs.
lines.but: Testing for kratom varied and was not recorded, so some deaths with kratom were probably missed.
how: A CDC system gathered 27,338 overdose deaths from 27 US states, July 2016 to December 2017. Kratom was found in 152.
Kratom was named as a cause in 91 deaths. Other drugs turned up in 84 of them; fentanyl was named as a cause in 51.
Only 7 deaths had kratom as the only drug found. Even then, the report says other drugs cannot be ruled out.
The system counts mostly deaths where opioids played a part. With no count of people who use kratom, there is no death rate.

cards.statement: In death records from 27 US states, most deaths where kratom was named as a cause had no other drug found.
Kratom shows up in a large share of US overdose deaths.

questions: Can a fentanyl strip show fentanyl when there is none?

lines.short: Sometimes. Large amounts of meth, MDMA or two medicines made strips positive with no fentanyl there.
lines.but: These were lab tests, mostly of one drug at a time. How often it happens when people test their own drugs is not known.
how: Of 104 seized samples in which a lab machine found no fentanyl, 6 still read positive on the strip.
In the lab, strong solutions of meth or MDMA turned strips positive. So did two medicines, diphenhydramine and lidocaine. Cocaine and several other drugs did not.
It took thousands of times more of these drugs than the smallest amount of fentanyl the same strips could find.

With take-home strips, 28 in 100 crystal meth samples showed fentanyl, against 5 in 100 other samples tested on site by staff. The authors think most were false positives. No lab checked these results.

cards.statement: Large amounts of meth or MDMA can make a fentanyl strip show fentanyl when there is none.

questions: Do fentanyl strips pick up drugs related to fentanyl, like carfentanil?

lines.short: In lab tests, strips found most related drugs, but not all. Carfentanil needed large amounts.
lines.but: These were mostly pure drugs in water, tested by lab staff. The largest study reported no repeat tests.
how: One lab tested 28 related drugs on four brands. At high amounts, 21 to 24 of them showed up.
At lower amounts, only 5 to 12 of the 23 tested showed up.
Three never showed up on any brand. Carfentanil showed only at high amounts, and never on one brand.
A second lab found 11 of 13 related drugs on all five batches of one brand. On two of the three newer batches, carfentanil showed only in very large amounts.

cards.statement: Fentanyl test strips can miss some drugs related to fentanyl, like carfentanil.

questions: Do all fentanyl strips work the same?

lines.short: No. In lab tests, brands and batches differed. Some batches needed ten times more fentanyl.
lines.but: Each difference comes from one or two lab studies, and why batches differed is not known.
how: Batches of one brand bought in 2021 needed ten times more fentanyl to show it than batches bought in 2017.
With no fentanyl there, the 2021 batches read positive with 10 to 40 times less lidocaine or MDMA than the 2017 batches.
Four brands picked up different numbers of related drugs. The one that found the most at a low amount never showed carfentanil. It also read positive with large amounts of vitamin C alone.

Two weeks of heat did not change one kind of strip. Strips more than four years out of date still worked, but needed more fentanyl than their label said. No new strips of that kind were tested to compare.

cards.statement: All fentanyl test strips work about the same, whatever the brand or batch.
In lab tests, one brand of fentanyl test strip read positive with large amounts of vitamin C alone.

questions: Do colour tests like Marquis show whether a pill has MDMA in it?

lines.short: In a lab, experts got MDMA right. Two first-time testers made many mistakes.
lines.but: One small lab study from 2003, with a kit and pills of that time.
how: Three lab experts read all 35 samples with MDMA as positive, and nearly all of the 4 without MDMA as negative.
Seven MDMA samples also had another drug, like caffeine or amphetamine. The colour looked the same.
Two people new to the kit tested 8 known drugs. One missed both MDMA samples. The other called four other drugs MDMA.
A review says MDA and MDEA, drugs close to MDMA, give a similar colour. It adds that, read by eye, the tests do not show how much MDMA a pill holds.

cards.statement: Colour test kits for MDMA are easy to read, even for first-timers.
If a colour test shows MDMA, the pill has nothing else in it.

questions: Do people throw drugs away when a test shows something unexpected?

lines.short: Sometimes. At one festival, 67 in 100 people handed over drugs that were not as sold.
lines.but: That was one festival, where chemists tested the drugs. After a strip showed fentanyl, few did.
how: At an English festival in 2016, 30 of 45 people whose drug was not as sold handed drugs over to be destroyed.
When the drug matched, 15 of 164 did. Staff saw these handovers, but people may have kept other drugs.
At a supervised injection site, people said they would throw the drug away after 11 in 100 checks that showed fentanyl, and after 7 in 100 that did not.
A review of drug checking services printed rates of 0 to 10 in 100 from four studies.

cards.statement: Most people throw their drugs away when a fentanyl test strip shows fentanyl.
When testing at one festival showed a drug wasn't as sold, most people handed drugs over to be destroyed.

questions: Did drug checking at a festival mean fewer hospital visits?

lines.short: We can't tell. Fewer people were taken to hospital for drugs, but other things changed too.
lines.but: One festival, one year before and one after, with no festival to compare.
how: At an English festival in 2016, chemists tested drugs on site for the first time.
People taken into hospital because of drugs: 19 in 2015 and 1 in 2016.
Other hospital admissions rose from 40 to 49, and paramedics were said to treat more people on site.
The author says the study cannot show what part the testing played.

cards.statement: At one English festival, drug-related hospital cases fell from 19 to 1 the year on-site testing began.

questions: Can test kits do harm by making people feel falsely safe?

lines.short: No study has measured this. Riskier use after a positive strip was rare when asked.
lines.but: The studies said little about what people did after a strip showed no fentanyl.
how: In one programme, 6 of 336 answers described riskier use after a strip showed fentanyl.
Some people misread strips, and strips do not show other drugs, such as xylazine.
With take-home strips, people found fentanyl in 28 in 100 meth samples, against 5 in 100 tested by staff.
Critics worry that a negative result could make people feel safe when they are not. This has not been measured.

cards.statement: Fentanyl test strips do not show other drugs, such as xylazine.

questions: Does a second dose work like the first?

lines.short: A second dose raises the drug in your blood, but not the strongest feeling.
lines.but: Three small laboratory studies, 9 to 23 people, and none gave more than two doses.
how: Blood levels rose more than the extra dose alone explains: MDMA slows its own breakdown.
The strongest feeling was no stronger after the second dose, but it lasted about an hour longer.
Heart rate hardly rose further, while blood pressure and body temperature did.
No study worked out how much effect a given blood level should give.

questions: What does a second dose do to the heart and body?

lines.short: Taking more adds strain on the heart and blood pressure without stronger good feelings.
lines.but: Small laboratory studies of healthy, screened people sitting in a quiet room.
how: After a second dose, 8 of 9 men went above a raised blood-pressure line, against 6 of 9.
Both cases of a racing heart in that study came after the second dose.
In another study, all ten men went above that line.
Nobody has tested hot, crowded places or the larger amounts people describe.

questions: Is the change bigger in people who have used more?

lines.short: People who had taken more ecstasy showed less of the serotonin marker.
lines.but: The amounts come from memory, and people who take more ecstasy take more of everything else.
how: Four studies found this link; two smaller ones did not.
In one, each doubling of pills went with a small further drop.
In another, years of use and the biggest dose went with the lowest levels.
Nobody measured how much people really took, or what was in the pills.

cards.statement: People who had taken more ecstasy showed less of a serotonin marker, in most studies.

questions: What happened when people with schizophrenia were given ketamine in a study?

lines.short: In nine patients, symptoms rose for twenty minutes, then returned to their usual level.
lines.but: Nine people, one study, and staff chose the order of the days instead of leaving it to chance.
how: Nine inpatients with schizophrenia, all taking an antipsychotic medicine, had four days: a dummy injection (placebo) and three amounts of ketamine. Two of them never got the largest amount, because staff held it back.
Twenty minutes after the two larger amounts, their symptom scores were higher than after the dummy injection.
What they described often repeated their own illness: suspicion, delusions, hallucinations and muddled thinking. Their overall scores were back to their usual level an hour and a half later.
Four of the nine said symptoms came back hours later, which nobody had expected or measured.

cards.statement: Given ketamine in one study, people with schizophrenia often described experiences that repeated their own illness.

questions: Can cannabis cause a sudden death?

lines.short: These studies do not settle that question.
lines.but: The linked deaths are selected reports with no comparison group.
how: A review collected 13 deaths linked to recent use. Eight had significant heart disease or other illness; five lacked a blood test showing recent use.
Larger studies, relayed by the review, point both ways. Some found no increase in deaths.
A Finnish table prints 0% as poisonings mainly attributed to THC, rounded to whole percent. That does not prove an exact zero count.
The reviewers encourage counting cannabis as a contributor in appropriate cases, but give no estimate of missed deaths.

cards.statement: No death has ever been linked to recent cannabis use.

questions: Do some people feel LSD more strongly than others?

lines.short: In lab studies, the dose went most with how strong LSD felt. Mood and personality did too.
lines.but: The paper says which way each link goes, not how big it is.
how: 213 healthy adults took LSD in a hospital room and, in most studies, a dummy pill on another day.
People who felt well just before had stronger effects than others. People who felt anxious had more anxiety during the session.
Open people had more spiritual feelings. People who had used drugs like LSD more often felt less overall than people who had used them less.
People whose genes make a liver enzyme slower had more LSD in the blood. Each session had one fixed dose, so taking more was not tested.

cards.statement: In lab studies, people who felt anxious just before taking LSD had more anxiety during the session.

questions: Do genes and the home you grow up in shape drug problems?

lines.short: Both are linked: what comes from birth parents, and the home a child grows up in.
lines.but: One Swedish study. What birth parents pass on includes the pregnancy, not just genes.
how: In Sweden, 18,115 adopted children born 1950 to 1993 were followed in health, prescription and court records until 2009.
Some birth parents had a drug problem on record. Their children, raised by adoptive parents, had one about twice as often: about 9 in 100, against 4 in 100 when neither birth parent did.
Adoptive brothers and sisters are not related by birth. Still, 6 in 100 of them had a drug problem when the adopted child had one, against 3 in 100 when the child did not.

The study did not work out a share due to genes. Where studies give one, it is about differences between people in one place and time. It does not say how much of your own risk comes from genes, and it can change when living conditions change.

cards.statement: In a Swedish study, adoptive brothers and sisters, not related by birth, more often had drug problems when the adopted child did.
Children adopted away from a birth parent with a drug problem still have drug problems more often.

questions: What did the 'Rat Park' studies show about environment and morphine?
What did the 'Rat Park' studies show about environment and drugs?

lines.short: Less than is often said. Rats living together drank less morphine water, but only in some tests.
lines.but: All of this was in rats, so it says nothing direct about people.
how: In 1979, by the last test, rats kept alone drank 5 to over 16 times as much sweet morphine water as rats living together.
In 1978, when morphine water was almost all they had to drink, the rats living together drank more of it.
In all three studies, the two groups drank morphine water from different machines, measured differently. That could explain part of the gap.
Two later experiments meant to repeat the 1981 Rat Park morphine study did not find the same result.

cards.statement: In the 1978 Rat Park study, rats living together refused morphine water.
Rat Park has been repeated, with the same result.

questions: What is meth withdrawal like, and how long does it last?

lines.short: After stopping, most symptoms people reported eased within one to two weeks. Low mood and craving lasted longer.
lines.but: It was one small study on a hospital ward. The people in it were not seeking treatment.
how: People dependent on meth stopped using on a hospital research ward.
Most symptoms they reported eased within one to two weeks.
Low mood lasted about three weeks; craving lasted to week five, at a lower level.
They were not looking for treatment. None had another mental-health diagnosis at the time.

cards.statement: In one small study, most symptoms of stopping meth eased within one to two weeks.
Meth cravings go away as quickly as the other withdrawal symptoms.

questions: Does exercise help low mood and worry after stopping meth?

lines.short: In one trial, exercise went with slightly less sadness and worry than health classes.
lines.but: Both groups got much better, and people knew their group, so hope may explain part.
how: People in a live-in treatment centre were put by chance into exercise or health classes.
Every week they filled in questionnaires about sadness and worry.
Both groups improved a lot; the exercise group improved a little more.
The exercise group started out more worried, which can make a bigger drop look like an effect.

cards.statement: In one trial, people in meth treatment felt much less sad and worried whether they did exercise or health classes.

questions: How do mood, craving and sleep change after stopping cocaine?

lines.short: In a closed research unit, men's low mood and craving were worst on the first day and eased over the next weeks.
lines.but: Only 12 men were studied, in a place with no cocaine and nothing to remind them of it.
how: The men were compared with 10 men with no history of drug problems, living in the same unit.
Most of the improvement came in the first two weeks.
Their reported sleep was much like the other men's, except that falling asleep was harder and feeling clear-headed on waking improved more.
An older study of people stopping at home described craving coming back after a few calm days.

cards.statement: An older study of people stopping cocaine at home described craving coming back after a few calm days.

questions: After high doses of DXM, how long is balance affected?

lines.short: After the highest doses, balance and coordination were still affected at the day's last test, while other effects were wearing off.
lines.but: Testing stopped there, so nobody knows when it ended, and nobody was tested next day.
how: Twelve experienced volunteers took DXM, a sleeping pill or a dummy pill on different days.
They did balance and button-pressing tests several times each day.
DXM affected these tests for longer than the sleeping pill did.
More than half vomited at least once at the higher doses.

questions: A month after high doses of DXM, any lasting effects?

lines.short: A month later, no one reported lasting upset or lasting changes in what they saw or heard.
lines.but: Only 12 carefully chosen volunteers, in a calm lab; people with psychosis or bipolar illness, themselves or in close family, could not take part.
how: Twelve prepared volunteers had DXM, a sleeping pill or a dummy pill on different days.
They came back about a month after their last session and filled in a questionnaire.
They also reported good changes, but the questionnaire could not separate DXM days from the other days.
One person asked not to have that dose again; they had a headache after the session that they put down to DXM.

questions: Does using ketamine often affect memory, even days later?

lines.short: On some memory tests, people who used ketamine most days did worse than others.
lines.but: They also had less schooling. Nobody was tested before they started.
how: A London team tested people who used ketamine more than four times a week. The tests were a day or a few days after they last used it.
They made more mistakes when asked to remember which boxes they had already looked in. They also knew fewer of the patterns they had seen. This was compared with people who used other drugs or none.
They did as well at remembering a story and finding words. People who used ketamine a few times a month did as well too, though a smaller study found lower scores three days after a night out.
A year later, their scores were closer to the others', though most still used ketamine.

questions: What does ketamine do to memory and attention while it is working?

lines.short: People remembered far fewer words than on their salt-water day. An hour after it stopped, scores matched.
lines.but: Small studies, 14 to 18 people each, and no study checked that the raters stayed unaware.
how: The same people were tested twice: once with ketamine in a vein, once with salt water.
With ketamine they recalled and recognised fewer words, and were a little slower to notice a repeated word.
Two of the three studies tested again after the drip stopped. About an hour later, scores matched the salt-water day.
Counts like 13 of 15 compare each person with their own score before the drug, not with their salt-water day.

questions: Can sniffing solvents cause sudden death?

lines.short: Sudden deaths after sniffing solvents and sprays were reported in one old survey.
lines.but: It counted deaths, without measuring risk among everyone who used these products.
how: A 1969 US survey described 110 deaths among young people aged 11 to 23, mostly involving sprays or a cleaning solvent. The report did not list poppers.
In several witnessed deaths, the person suddenly ran or panicked before collapsing. Where autopsies were described, they found no other cause.
The author proposed an effect on the heart's rhythm. No heart trace was recorded.
Families or friends hid the sniffing in 8 deaths, so some other deaths may have been missed.

questions: Is using ecstasy in pregnancy linked to birth defects?

lines.short: One study counted birth defects after ecstasy in pregnancy, but it cannot show cause.
lines.but: There was no comparison group, and almost half of the enquiries were lost to follow-up.
how: A UK information service followed 136 pregnancies in which ecstasy was used, nearly all in the first 3 months. 62 of them also involved other drugs.
Of 78 babies born alive, 12 (about 15 in 100) had a birth defect, a mix of minor and major ones. The authors expected 2 to 3 in 100.
Two babies had heart defects and three had a twisted foot. The authors say the study is too small to confirm a link with any one defect.

A later study followed babies of 28 women who used ecstasy but did not report a count of birth defects. One baby had a rare genetic condition, which the authors say cannot be tied to the mother's drug use.

cards.statement: In one study, more babies exposed to ecstasy in pregnancy had birth defects than expected.

questions: How do babies exposed to ecstasy in pregnancy do in their first months?

lines.short: At 1 and 4 months, babies of women who used ecstasy mostly scored the same.
lines.but: The mothers also used more cocaine, cannabis, tobacco and alcohol, and only 22 exposed babies were seen.
how: 28 women used ecstasy in or just before pregnancy. Their babies were compared with babies of 68 women who used other drugs but not ecstasy in pregnancy.
At 1 month, average scores did not differ. Two patterns leaned toward more low-energy behavior (91 in 100 against 73 in 100) and less stiffness (9 against 27).

At 4 months, one movement-quality rating was lower in exposed babies (average 59 against 74), and more of them were boys (71 in 100 against 46 in 100). Mental and other movement scores were about the same.
The authors say heavier use went with lower scores. That compares only 13 heavier-use mothers with 15 lighter-use mothers, and the lighter-use babies scored above unexposed babies on two scales.

questions: Is cannabis linked to heart attacks and strokes?

lines.short: Some studies link it to heart attacks and strokes; a 25-year study found no link.
lines.but: These figures come from reviews. The studies could not fully tell cannabis and tobacco apart.
how: In one study, a heart attack was more likely to start in the hour after using cannabis. Only a few people had used it in that hour.
Two surveys found more strokes, mostly in people who used cannabis every week or more.
A study that followed young adults for over 25 years found no link with heart disease or stroke.
The American Heart Association said the evidence is not yet clear.

questions: How many opioid deaths also involve benzodiazepines?

lines.short: About 1 in 5 US opioid overdose deaths in 2017 also involved benzos.
lines.but: Death records miss some drugs, and a share of deaths does not measure risk.
how: US death certificates listed benzos in 21 of 100 opioid overdose deaths in 2017, up from 9 in 1999.
Benzos were listed more often with prescription opioids or methadone (about 1 in 3) than with heroin or fentanyl.
In North Carolina in 2010, medical examiners, who investigate deaths, judged benzos involved in about 6 in 10 deaths involving an opioid painkiller.
Of people on prescribed opioids who died of overdose, half (US veterans) to three in four (Ontario) had benzo prescriptions.

cards.statement: Among people on prescribed opioids who died of overdose, half to three in four also had benzo prescriptions.
Benzos were listed in about 1 in 5 US opioid overdose deaths in 2017.

questions: On methadone or buprenorphine and also prescribed sedatives?

lines.short: In UK methadone or buprenorphine treatment, benzo prescriptions were linked to more poisoning deaths.
lines.but: The study did not take mental health, alcohol or street drug use into account.
how: Poisoning deaths were about 1 in 100 people per year with a benzo prescription, and 1 in 200 without.
The link was stronger when benzo doses were above the highest dose the UK drug guide advises.
Sleeping tablets called z-drugs were also linked to poisoning deaths, though deaths were few.
People prescribed benzos stayed in treatment longer, but the link with poisoning deaths was still there.

cards.statement: In UK methadone or buprenorphine treatment, people also prescribed benzos died of poisoning more often.

questions: Opioids with gabapentin or pregabalin: how much riskier?

lines.short: Gabapentin or pregabalin with opioid painkillers was linked to more opioid overdose deaths in Ontario.
lines.but: Both Ontario studies are from one team and do not say why people were given the medicines.
how: In Ontario, 12 in 100 people who died had a recent gabapentin prescription, against 7 in 100 similar living people.
For pregabalin it was about 5 in 100 people who died, against 3 in 100 similar living people.
After allowing for opioid dose and other medicines, the odds of an opioid death were about 1.5 times higher with gabapentin and 1.7 times with pregabalin.
In UK methadone or buprenorphine treatment, gabapentin-type medicines were not clearly linked to poisoning deaths; deaths were few.

cards.statement: In Ontario studies, gabapentin or pregabalin taken with opioid painkillers was linked to more opioid overdose deaths.

questions: Does meth taken during the day spoil that night's sleep?

lines.short: After one of the larger doses, people slept less and worse that night than after a dummy dose.
lines.but: This was one small hospital study with single doses, not binges.
how: Each person had a dummy dose (placebo) and three real doses, on different days.
A wrist monitor measured sleep in 6 people; all 11 said how they had slept.
With the biggest dose, the monitor showed about two hours less sleep than with the dummy dose, and more waking than with any other dose.
People felt their sleep was even shorter and worse than the monitor showed.

cards.statement: In one small study, people slept about two hours less after the biggest meth dose than after a dummy dose.

questions: How do you feel the morning after one dose of meth?

lines.short: Next morning, the biggest dose left people less alert and friendly than a dummy dose.
lines.but: Memory tests showed no change, but the study was small and printed no test results.
how: Eleven people took a dummy dose and real doses on different days in a hospital unit.
Next morning they rated their mood and did memory and attention tests.
After the biggest dose, their heart beat faster and blood pressure was higher than after the dummy dose.
They did not feel sadder or more worried, or want meth more.

cards.statement: In a small study, the biggest meth dose left heart rate and blood pressure higher the next morning than a dummy dose.
One dose of meth leaves people sadder and craving it the next morning.

questions: Does MDMA spoil sleep that night?

lines.short: After MDMA, people slept about two hours less than with a dummy pill, and had very little dreaming (REM) sleep.
lines.but: Only 7 people, one dose, in a quiet sleep lab, not a night out.
how: Seven people slept in a sleep lab after MDMA one night and after a dummy pill another night.
After MDMA they took much longer to fall asleep than after the dummy pill.
Dreaming (REM) sleep almost disappeared that night, then came back the next night.
A short night without MDMA did not remove dreaming sleep in the same way.

cards.statement: After MDMA in a sleep lab, dreaming (REM) sleep almost disappeared that night, then came back the next night.

questions: Are you sleepier the day after MDMA?

lines.short: We don't know: next-day sleepiness after MDMA was not clearly different from a dummy pill.
lines.but: Only 7 people were tested, too few to rule out a difference.
how: The next day, people lay down for short naps to see how fast they fell asleep.
After a short night in bed, they fell asleep faster than after a full night with the dummy pill.
After MDMA, they took about as long to fall asleep as after the dummy pill.
They were not asked how tired they felt, and mood and thinking were not tested the next day.

questions: What is the cocaine crash, and how long does it last?

lines.short: After a binge, people described a crash: very low mood, then long, heavy sleep and hunger.
lines.but: This is what some people in treatment told their doctors; it cannot show how often it happens.
how: Doctors talked with 30 people who came for help with heavy cocaine use; there was no comparison group.
The crash began soon after the last use and usually ended within a few days.
Some people had passing thoughts of suicide, which were limited to the crash.
Many had used alcohol or other drugs to get to sleep.

cards.statement: People who sought help for heavy cocaine use said the crash after a binge usually ended within a few days.

questions: How do you feel the day after taking ecstasy?

lines.short: People felt very tired and had slept less, but were not sadder than others.
lines.but: Two small studies; nobody tested the pills or measured sleep with a machine.
how: In London, 12 people who took ecstasy at a club were compared with 12 people who only drank alcohol.
The next day the ecstasy group felt much more tired and low on energy, and did worse at a sums test.
In Melbourne, people who took ecstasy slept about two hours less than people who use ecstasy but skipped it that week.
In both studies, mood the next day was about the same as in the other group.

cards.statement: In two small studies, people felt much sadder the day after ecstasy than others did.

questions: Do most US dollar bills carry traces of cocaine?

lines.short: In one US study, about 9 in 10 one-dollar bills had traces of cocaine. The typical bill held a little over a millionth of a gram.
lines.but: One small study of 50 US one-dollar bills collected by 2000. Cocaine on money today, or elsewhere, may differ.
how: The bills came from everyday purchases, 10 each in Baltimore, Chicago, Denver, Honolulu and San Juan. Only 4, all from Chicago, had no cocaine.
One bill from Honolulu held about 7 in 10 of all the cocaine found. So the average was far above what most bills held.
A few bills also carried heroin (7 of 50), methamphetamine (3) or PCP (2).

questions: Can touching fentanyl make you overdose?

lines.short: Poison experts call it very unlikely for police and paramedics, and no overdose from touching fentanyl has been confirmed. In 214 news stories about exposed responders, none had proof.

how: Poison experts did sums from fentanyl skin patches, made to deliver it. Powder on skin, they argue, is taken up more slowly and can be washed off.

Poison experts say fentanyl splashed into the eyes or mouth is no real risk.

questions: Do memory and thinking differences last after people stop using cannabis?

In Australia, 469 people dependent on meth reported violent crime in 12 of 100 months with meth use and 3 of 100 without.
That study compared each person with themselves. But people reported use and crime for the same months.

cards.statement: In one study, people dependent on meth reported more violent crime in months they used it.

questions: Do bupropion or modafinil help people stop using meth?

lines.short: Bupropion and modafinil did not help more people stop than a dummy pill.
lines.but: The trials were small, so a modest benefit or harm cannot be ruled out.
how: Putting five trials together: about 1 in 5 had stopped by the end, on medicine or on a dummy pill.
The trials were small and uneven, so a modest benefit or harm can't be ruled out.
A later review of bupropion found about a tenth fewer positive urine tests. This result is uncertain.

cards.statement: Bupropion and modafinil have been shown to help people stop using meth.

questions: Have any medicines been shown to help meth psychosis?

lines.short: Few trials have tested medicines for meth psychosis: eight small, short ones and one longer one.
lines.but: None of the short trials had a dummy-pill group, so they can't show if medicines help more than stopping meth. Some have serious flaws.
how: Three reviews found eight small, short trials, with about 500 people in all.
Six compared one medicine with another. None was a clear winner.
Two small trials against a dummy pill, in people already getting better, and one two-year trial favoured the medicine on some measures. These trials have serious flaws.
Nobody has studied what happens when people stop the medicine.

questions: Have meth use and meth deaths risen in the US?

lines.short: In the US, meth use rose from 2015 to 2019, and deaths involving meth kept rising through 2023, the latest year counted.
lines.but: Many of these deaths also involved fentanyl or other opioids. The rise slowed after 2021.
how: In US surveys, past-year meth use rose by about a fifth from 2015 to 2019.
Deaths involving meth rose from about 550 in 1999 to about 35,000 in 2023. The rise slowed after 2021.
Medical examiners' reports from 2021 to mid-2024: about 7 in 10 overdose deaths involving meth also involved opioids. This is a different kind of record from the death counts.
The surveys miss people who are homeless or living in places like prisons and hospitals.

cards.statement: In most recent US overdose deaths involving meth, meth was the only drug.

questions: Is a serotonin by-product lower in people who use MDMA?

lines.short: In one study, a serotonin by-product in spinal fluid was lower in people who used MDMA.
lines.but: It was clear only in the women, and that group had used many other drugs too.
how: Thirty people who had used MDMA at least 25 times were compared with 28 who had not.
Their spinal fluid held about a third less of a serotonin by-product.
The gap was clear in the women and not in the men, and it did not grow with more use.
A lower level of a by-product cannot show that nerve cells were harmed.

questions: Are lower memory scores due to ecstasy, or to other drugs?

lines.short: In people who used ecstasy but hardly any other drug, memory scores were no different.
lines.but: It was one study, and medium-sized differences could not be ruled out.
how: 52 people who used ecstasy were compared with 59 people from the same all-night dance scene.
Breath, urine and hair tests checked that they had used little else.
Memory scores did not differ, and most of the 40 measures were similar.
People who had used it more than 50 times did worse on one planning test.

cards.statement: People who use ecstasy score worse on memory tests even if they use hardly any other drug.

questions: Does memory change when people start using ecstasy?

lines.short: In one Dutch study, people who started using ecstasy improved less on a word-memory test.
lines.but: They also used more cannabis and cocaine, and were tested again sooner.
how: Young people were tested before they had ever used ecstasy, then again 1 to 2 years later.
Those who started had used very little by the second test.
They improved less at learning a word list; nine other scores did not differ.
Everyone's scores stayed in the normal range.

questions: Is meth use linked to crime?

lines.short: People dependent on meth reported more crime in months when they used it.
lines.but: One study, and it could not show which came first.
how: In Australia, 469 people dependent on meth were followed for up to three years. Each person's months with meth were compared with their own months without.
Some crime was reported in 56 of 100 months with meth use and about 18 of 100 without.
The link was strongest for selling drugs and property crime. It stayed after other drug use and money and housing problems were counted.
People reported use and crime for the same months, and treatment or time in prison was not counted.

cards.statement: In one study, violent crime was the crime most tied to months of meth use.

questions: Could people in the trials tell if they got MDMA?

lines.short: In the trial that asked, most people could tell MDMA from the dummy pill.
lines.but: Only one of the two trials asked, and only at the very end.
how: At the end of the second trial, 94 in 100 people on MDMA and 75 in 100 on the dummy pill guessed right.
About 8 in 10 people on MDMA were sure they had it. One person stopped because they thought they had the dummy pill.
The first trial did not ask. Critics say up to 9 in 10 people there may have guessed right.
Neither trial reports measuring what people expected, so we cannot tell how much of the gain came from MDMA itself.

cards.statement: In the MDMA trial for PTSD that asked, most people could tell MDMA from the dummy pill.

questions: What side effects did MDMA cause in the PTSD trials?

lines.short: MDMA often gave brief side effects, like tight muscles, feeling sick and sweating.
lines.but: The trials were too small and short to show rare or later harms.
how: In two trials, 99 people took MDMA and 95 took a dummy pill, with therapy. No serious side effects were seen on MDMA.
Tight muscles affected about 59 to 63 in 100 people on MDMA, against 11 to 26 in 100 on the dummy pill.
In each session on MDMA, the top blood pressure number reached 160 or more in up to 22 in 100 people, against 4 in 100 on the dummy pill.
Feeling very happy was written down only if people mentioned it, and there were no heart tracings or blood tests after the doses.

questions: Why were three earlier MDMA therapy studies withdrawn?

lines.short: In 2024 a journal withdrew three earlier studies from the MDMA therapy research.
lines.but: The journal did not say how much of the data came from that site.
how: The three studies came from the earlier, smaller trials of the same research programme.
The journal said the authors knew of serious rule-breaking at one study site, did not tell it, and had not fully declared their ties to the sponsor.
The company's own papers, written two months before, say one person in that study was seriously harmed by sexual misconduct.
Most of the authors who answered the journal disagreed with the withdrawals.

cards.statement: In 2024, a journal withdrew three MDMA therapy studies, saying the authors had not told it of serious rule-breaking at one site.

questions: Is MDMA therapy good value for money?

lines.short: Two critics say price and comparison decide if MDMA therapy is good value.
lines.but: The cost studies come from the company or from people with money ties to it.
how: The company's study compared MDMA therapy with the same talking therapy plus a dummy pill.
The critics, who also have money ties to the company, say it should be compared with the treatments people would otherwise get.
At the company's price, the critics' model needs about 8 years before savings cover the cost; at a much lower price it could save money.
The company's papers for the regulator give no results on health-care use, and no independent study was among the papers read.

questions: Does the benefit of MDMA therapy for PTSD last?

lines.short: Months to years later, people who had MDMA still scored lower on PTSD.
lines.but: Only about 7 in 10 came back for one check, and many had other treatments in between.
how: One check-up visit scored PTSD again, 6 months to over 2 years after the trials.
137 of 195 people came back, and those who came back had done better at the end of the trials.
Of those checked, about 7 in 10 who had MDMA and 3 in 10 who had the dummy pill still had no PTSD, the company says.
People from the first trial knew which pill they had, and the US regulator said this visit was not set up to show if the benefit lasts.

questions: Does MDMA therapy help people with alcohol problems?

lines.short: In one small study, 9 of 14 people drank much less after MDMA therapy.
lines.but: There was no group without MDMA. And all had just been through detox.
how: 14 adults with alcohol use disorder, all just out of detox, had ten therapy sessions. Two of them included MDMA.
Three months later, 9 of the 14 said they were drinking much less than at the start.
The start seems to have been before detox, so a big drop was likely anyway.
People reported their own drinking. No study we read compared people who had MDMA with people who did not.

questions: Does MDMA therapy help couples where one partner has PTSD?

lines.short: After couples therapy with MDMA, PTSD eased and couples were happier.
lines.but: Neither study had a group without MDMA. And this couples therapy helps PTSD even without it.
how: Two small studies, 14 couples in all, added two MDMA sessions to couples therapy for PTSD.
PTSD scores dropped a lot after treatment. Both partners felt happier together.
In the second study, part of the gain faded by 6 months, and one partner felt worse.
No one had a serious side effect. Without a comparison group, we cannot tell what MDMA added.

cards.statement: MDMA has been tried in couples therapy for PTSD, and both partners felt happier together afterwards.

questions: Does MDMA therapy help depression?

lines.short: In one small study, depression dropped a lot after two MDMA sessions.
lines.but: There was no group without MDMA. And the people who scored depression knew everyone had taken it.
how: 12 adults in Norway with depression had two MDMA sessions. They also had talking therapy before and after.
About two months later, depression scores had fallen from about 30 to about 10, and 9 of the 12 were much better.
No one had a serious side effect. But 4 to 6 of the 12 had worse thoughts of suicide at some point. 2 needed medicine for anxiety and sleep.
Most people signed up on their own. So many probably expected to get better.

cards.statement: In a small MDMA study for depression, 4 to 6 of 12 people had worse thoughts of suicide at some point.

questions: Did MDMA therapy for PTSD change people's drinking or drug use?

lines.short: MDMA therapy for PTSD did not clearly change drinking or drug use.
lines.but: Almost no one had a drinking or drug problem to start with. And people reported their own use.
how: In one PTSD trial, 82 people filled in forms about alcohol and drugs. They did this before and after treatment with MDMA or a dummy pill.
Drinking scores fell by 1 point with MDMA and rose slightly with the dummy pill, on a scale of 0 to 40.
The MDMA group started with higher scores. Allowing for that, the difference could be chance.
Drug-use scores went down a little in both groups.

questions: What side effects did MDMA cause in trials outside PTSD?

lines.short: In small trials, MDMA's side effects were common and brief, and none were serious.
lines.but: These trials were too small to show rare or later harms.
how: Five small studies gave MDMA to 58 people. They had anxiety, depression, social anxiety with autism, or PTSD in couples.
A tight jaw, thirst, sweating and headache were common during sessions. Tiredness was common in the week after.
Blood pressure, pulse and body heat went up during sessions. None of this needed treatment.
Thoughts of suicide were recorded as side effects in a few people; in one trial this was as common with the dummy pill.

cards.statement: In small MDMA trials, tiredness was common in the week after a session.

questions: In the early MDMA trials for PTSD, did the benefit last?

lines.short: In two sets of early PTSD trials, average PTSD scores stayed about as low as at the end of MDMA therapy a year or more later.
lines.but: There was no comparison group, many people also had other therapy or medicines, and the same sponsor ran both studies.
how: In one small trial, 16 of 19 people were checked again about 4 years later, and their average score had hardly changed.
Some people got much better and some much worse; 2 had moderate-to-severe PTSD again.
In four other trials, scores a year later were a little lower than at the end of treatment, after everyone had had full doses.
Those results had to be corrected after an ethics breach by two therapists at one site.

questions: Does MDMA therapy for PTSD change sleep?

lines.short: In early PTSD trials, people who had full doses of MDMA said they slept better than people who had a very small dose.
lines.but: The trials were small, no one checked whether people could tell which dose they had, and the results had to be corrected after an ethics breach at one site.
how: On a 0 to 21 sleep scale, scores improved by about 4 points more with full doses, a month or two after treatment.
About half of the full-dose group improved by 3 points or more, against 2 of 14 in the small-dose group.
A year later sleep was a little better still, but by then everyone had had full doses, so there was nothing to compare with.

questions: How was MDMA used in therapy before it was banned?

lines.short: Before MDMA was banned in 1985, a few dozen US therapists used it in talking therapy.
lines.but: This comes second-hand from one history review, and the reports of the time were not designed well enough to show whether MDMA helped.
how: Therapists reported good results, and a follow-up of 29 patients found no serious side effects.
Two therapists had sexual contact with patients during sessions and lost their licences.
A US judge said the strictest ban was not needed, but the drug agency imposed it anyway.
Research applications were then blocked for years; the first approved study, in healthy people, began in 1992.

cards.statement: A US judge said the strictest ban on MDMA was not needed, but the drug agency imposed it anyway.

questions: Do brain scans change when people first start using ecstasy?

lines.short: In one study, a few pills did not change the serotonin marker.
lines.but: Most of these people had taken only one or two pills in all.
how: Young people were scanned before they had ever used ecstasy, then about 17 months later.
Before anyone started, the two groups' scans looked the same.
After starting, the serotonin marker and the brain chemicals had not changed.
A few other brain measures differed, each by less than five in a hundred.

cards.statement: In one study, a few ecstasy pills did not change a serotonin marker in young people scanned before and after.

questions: What can MDMA do to the kidneys?

lines.short: Kidney injury after MDMA has been reported in single cases; nobody knows how often.
lines.but: This is second-hand, from reviews of case reports, which cannot show how often it happens.
how: Most reported cases followed muscle breakdown after fits, very hard physical exertion or overheating.
A few single cases had other routes, such as inflamed blood vessels, a blocked bladder outlet or very high blood pressure.
In 164 healthy volunteers who took MDMA once or twice in a laboratory, kidney blood tests about a month later were about the same as before; nobody tested them in the hours and days after.
No study compared amounts, so the reports cannot show whether taking more makes it more likely.

questions: Can regular heavy MDMA use harm the heart valves?

lines.short: Heart valve changes were more common in people who had taken MDMA, in one small study.
lines.but: Nobody was scanned before taking MDMA, so this cannot show that MDMA caused it.
how: 8 of 29 people who had taken MDMA for at least six months had valve findings that met a US definition of drug-related valve disease. None of 29 students who reported no drug use did.
The biggest gap was in the tricuspid valve, which that definition does not cover: 13 of 29 had a leak of grade 2 of 4 or more, against none. Most leaks were mild or moderate.

By their own account, the people had taken about 4 pills a week for about 6 years, on average. Those with higher leak grades said they had taken more in total, but the paper does not give the group sizes.
Other drug use is not reported, and the amounts came from what people said. The study says nothing about symptoms or illness.

cards.statement: In one small study, heart valve changes were more common in people who had taken MDMA for six months or more.

questions: Opioid painkillers with MAOI antidepressants?

lines.short: Reports link pethidine and tramadol to bad reactions with MAOI antidepressants; none for morphine.
lines.but: It rests on old case reports in reviews; nobody has counted how often it happens.
how: A 2005 review says pethidine, tramadol and dextromethorphan (in some cough medicines) were involved in reactions with MAOIs, an older kind of antidepressant. Some cases ended in death.
It found no reports for morphine, codeine, oxycodone or buprenorphine. That is a lack of reports, not a test in people. Fentanyl and methadone are unclear.
9 of the 11 papers it cites for deaths are from 1955 to 1971. The doctor thinks the risk is probably low but hard to predict.
Some people feel little pain relief from an amount and take more. No study looked at what happens then with an MAOI.

questions: Cannabis alone: are drivers who test positive more often in crashes?

lines.short: Drivers with cannabis in a test were linked to more crashes.
lines.but: These studies compare crashed drivers with others, so they cannot show one driver's chance of crashing.
how: Across 28 results from 21 studies in 13 countries, drivers with cannabis found in a test had about 1.2 to 1.4 times the odds of a crash, or of being at fault in one.
An older review found 1.9 times. Re-checking its counts and allowing for other factors brought the same studies to between 1.2 and 1.4.
Studies that allowed for alcohol found 1.1 to 1.2 times. Studies that did not found 1.7 to 1.8 times.
A positive test shows cannabis was in the body, not that a driver was impaired.

cards.statement: A positive cannabis test shows that a driver was impaired.
The link between cannabis and car crashes stays just as strong when studies allow for drinking.

questions: What does a hangover do to my thinking the next day?

lines.short: The morning after heavy drinking, people remembered less and reacted slower than on alcohol-free days.
lines.but: The studies were small, and a short night's sleep may explain part of it.
how: Researchers gave people memory, attention and speed tests the morning after a night of heavy drinking.
They compared the results with a day without alcohol, mostly in the same people.
One review gathered 19 of these studies and combined the numbers from 11.

cards.statement: The morning after heavy drinking, people remembered less and reacted more slowly than on alcohol-free days.

questions: Do I drive worse the morning after, even with no alcohol left?

lines.short: Young drivers in a lab driving test drove worse after drinking nights than after alcohol-free nights.
lines.but: It was a driving machine in a lab, not real roads, and nobody checked how much they slept.
how: 52 young drivers did a short pretend drive to work, twice.
Once the morning after a night out drinking, and once after a night without alcohol.
Half had no alcohol left in their breath, and they still drove worse.

cards.statement: If a breath test finds no alcohol left the morning after drinking, your driving is back to normal.

questions: Does drinking water while drinking alcohol stop a hangover?

lines.short: In one small test, men felt no better next morning when they had water between drinks than when they drank the same sake without it.
lines.but: Only 13 men took part, so a small benefit cannot be ruled out.
how: Each man drank the same sake twice: once with water in between, once without.
They rated headache, feeling sick and tiredness the next morning.
The company that made the sake paid for the study.

questions: Does drinking beer before wine, or wine before beer, change my hangover?

lines.short: Drinking beer before wine or wine before beer gave about the same hangover.
lines.but: Only one kind of beer and one white wine were tested.
how: Young adults drank beer and wine on two days, in a different order each time.
Doctors watched them, and they slept at the university.
Each person's hangover after one order was compared with their hangover after the other order.

questions: Do people who take hangover pills drink more?

lines.short: Young adults who had used hangover pills reported more drinking problems than those who never had.
lines.but: A one-time survey cannot show whether the pills cause heavier drinking.
how: 1312 young adults in Los Angeles who drink answered a survey.
Only 42 of them had ever used hangover pills.
Researchers compared their drinking with the people who had never used them.

questions: Does paracetamol at usual doses harm the liver in people who drink?

lines.short: In short trials, paracetamol at usual doses did not raise a liver test more than dummy pills; some trials saw small, short-lived rises later.
lines.but: Most people in the trials had just stopped heavy drinking, and no trial tested paracetamol for a hangover.
how: Five trials gave people who drink either paracetamol or a dummy pill.
Doctors checked a liver blood test, and nobody had liver failure.
The researchers had links to a paracetamol maker.

questions: Is there a medicine that makes amphetamine withdrawal easier?

lines.short: In the four trials reviewed, no medicine clearly eased withdrawal or craving more than a dummy pill.
lines.but: The review found only four small trials, so a small benefit could have been missed.
how: Four trials gave people starting treatment one of two medicines or a dummy pill (placebo).
One medicine helped people stay in treatment more than a dummy pill did, but it is no longer sold.
The other medicine did not help in the better trial; a smaller trial disagreed.
The review gave no side-effect results for any of the trials.

questions: How does sleep change in the weeks after stopping cocaine?

lines.short: Over three weeks off cocaine, measured sleep got worse while people felt they slept better.
lines.but: One small study of 20 people in a hospital unit; daytime light and withdrawal from other drugs were not controlled.
how: Twenty people with cocaine dependence slept in a sleep lab during their first weeks off cocaine.
Machines showed they took longer to fall asleep and slept less by the third week.
Dreaming (REM) sleep went down, while deep sleep went up a little.
Their own ratings of sleep got better, and were no worse than healthy men's.

cards.statement: In one study, sleep after stopping cocaine got better both on sleep-lab machines and in how people felt.

questions: Can the medicine modafinil help sleep after stopping cocaine?

lines.short: In one small trial, modafinil helped people fall asleep faster than a dummy pill did.
lines.but: Only 20 people in hospital, and side effects like headache were more common on modafinil.
how: Half of 20 people took modafinil and half a dummy pill, without knowing which.
Machines in a sleep lab measured their sleep on several nights over three weeks.
People on modafinil had more deep sleep than those on the dummy pill and, in the third week, more sleep overall.
They did not feel they slept better, and the study did not check whether it helped them stay off cocaine.

questions: Does the ADHD medicine methylphenidate cause sleep problems?

lines.short: Children on methylphenidate had sleep problems recorded more often than children on a dummy pill.
lines.but: The review says how many times more often, not how many children out of 100.
how: A review combined 35 trials in children and teenagers with ADHD.
Trouble falling asleep was recorded nearly three times as often with the medicine as with the dummy pill.
Who recorded sleep problems, and whether a questionnaire was used, changed how big the difference looked.
A drug company paid for the review, and two of the authors work for its parent company.

cards.statement: Children on the ADHD medicine methylphenidate had trouble falling asleep far more often than on a dummy pill.

questions: Can sleep medicines help when I stop alcohol, cannabis, cocaine or opioids?

lines.short: Some helped sleep, but better sleep did not reliably help people stay off drugs.
lines.but: This comes second-hand from a review that did not check how good the studies were.
how: Studies gave sleep medicines to people stopping a drug, some comparing them with a dummy pill.
For alcohol, gabapentin mostly helped, but in one big trial trazodone was linked with more drinking than a dummy pill.
For cannabis, several sleep medicines helped sleep, but none clearly helped people stay off it.
For opioids, trazodone did not help people on methadone sleep better.

questions: Can poppers damage your eyes?

lines.short: It seems so, in some people: reports describe blurry central vision and damage at the back of the eye.
lines.but: These are uncontrolled reports of people who saw an eye doctor, so they cannot prove poppers were the cause, or show how often it happens or which poppers do it.
how: Doctors in at least 12 countries have written about 113 people with eye problems after poppers, some after using them once.
Most had both eyes affected: blurry or dim vision in the middle, flashes of light, or a blank spot.
In most people scanned, the scans showed damage to the light-sensing cells at the centre of the retina, at the back of the eye.
Of the people who had a second scan, about 6 in 10 showed the damage improving or clearing.

cards.statement: Eye problems after poppers have only been reported after years of heavy use.
Scans of people with vision problems after poppers mostly showed damaged light-sensing cells at the back of the eye.

questions: Am I more likely to crash or fall when I start sleeping pills?

lines.short: Some studies found more crashes and falls soon after people started sleeping pills than without them; others did not.
lines.but: These studies watched what happened and cannot prove the pills caused the accidents.
how: Researchers compared people taking these pills with people not taking them.
The risk looked highest in the first weeks after starting.
Older people taking these pills had more falls than those not taking them.

cards.statement: In studies, older people taking sleeping pills had more falls than those not taking them.

questions: Does caffeine in the morning undo the effects of a sleeping pill?

lines.short: After a sleeping pill, morning caffeine left young men less sleepy than a dummy capsule did.
lines.but: Their test scores were not clearly better, and this study did not test driving.
how: 80 young men slept in a lab after a sleeping pill or a dummy pill.
In the morning they got either caffeine or a dummy capsule.

On four sleepiness measures taken together, the caffeine groups were less sleepy than matching groups given a dummy capsule; on the nap test alone, the difference was clear only after the higher flurazepam dose.

questions: Do people feel more anxious or low when hungover?

lines.short: People felt more anxious and low when hungover than when sober, and also described guilt.
lines.but: The review does not say how big the changes were, and poor sleep or regret may explain part of them.
how: One review gathered 22 studies with over 6,000 people, mostly young adults.
In most studies, people rated their mood when hungover and when sober or before drinking.
Most studies found worse mood when hungover, but two found no clear change in anxiety, at least for some people.

cards.statement: In studies, people felt more anxious and low when hungover from alcohol than when sober.

questions: Does anything help with the worry or low mood of a hangover?

lines.short: No study in the review tested a way to ease hangover worry; people said sharing the hangover with friends helped.
lines.but: These are people's own stories, not tests, so we cannot say what really helps.
how: Researchers interviewed about a hundred young adults about their hangovers.
Many felt bad about things they did while drunk or could not remember.
No study compared people who tried something with people who did not.

questions: What does drinking before bed do to my dream sleep?

lines.short: After drinking, dream sleep started later and was shorter than on nights without alcohol.
lines.but: These were small sleep-lab studies, and the results were not the same in every study.
how: Researchers measured sleep in a sleep lab with sensors on people's heads.
In most studies, the same people slept one night after alcohol and one night without it.
The more people drank, the more dream sleep they lost.

cards.statement: Alcohol before bed cuts dream sleep: it starts later and is shorter than on nights without alcohol.

questions: Does a drink help me fall asleep or sleep longer?

lines.short: On average, alcohol before bed did not help people fall asleep faster than on nights without alcohol.
lines.but: Whether it changes how long people sleep is unclear, because the studies disagreed.
how: 27 small sleep-lab studies were put together in one review.
On average, falling asleep took about the same time with or without alcohol.
Only after larger amounts was falling asleep a little quicker.
In three of five studies, people felt they fell asleep faster after alcohol.

cards.statement: On average, an alcoholic drink before bed helps people fall asleep faster.
In three of five studies, people felt they fell asleep faster after alcohol.

questions: Does caffeine during the day affect my sleep that night?

lines.short: After caffeine, people slept about 45 minutes less than on nights without caffeine.
lines.but: The people studied were healthy adults with low to moderate usual caffeine intake, so heavy users, teenagers and older adults may differ.
how: 24 studies compared nights after caffeine with nights without it, in the same people.
Caffeine made falling asleep slower, time awake in the night longer, and sleep lighter.
The more caffeine, and the closer to bedtime, the more sleep people lost.
In five studies, people did not report more time awake in the night.

cards.statement: Caffeine added time awake in the night, yet in five studies people did not report more time awake.
Caffeine doesn't really change how much you sleep that night.

questions: Can caffeine pills in hospital stop the headache after an operation?

lines.short: In one small trial, fewer patients given caffeine pills had headaches after surgery than patients given dummy pills.
lines.but: The trial was small, so it cannot show whether the pills are safe for everyone.
how: The patients were people who usually had a lot of caffeine every day.
Nurses gave either caffeine pills or identical dummy pills around the operation.
The amount and acidity of stomach fluid, which caffeine can raise, did not differ significantly between the groups.

cards.statement: In one small trial, caffeine pills around surgery meant fewer headaches afterwards for people who usually had lots of caffeine.

questions: What does stopping smoking feel like, and for how long?

lines.short: After stopping smoking, people can feel grumpy, anxious and restless, and wake more at night, for weeks.
lines.but: This comes from one expert's summary of older studies; it does not say how many people get each feeling.
how: The studies asked the same people how they felt before and after they stopped smoking.
Most of these feelings were strongest in the first week and gone within 2 to 4 weeks.
Feeling tired, headaches and sweating did not go up after stopping.
For some people the feelings lasted longer or came back after about three weeks.

cards.statement: In older studies, headaches and sweating went up after people stopped smoking.
The grumpiness and restlessness of quitting smoking usually last for months.

questions: Do ADHD medicines like methylphenidate make it harder for children to sleep?

lines.short: On stimulant medicine, children took longer to fall asleep and slept less than on nights without it, sleep monitors showed.
lines.but: The review did not say by how many minutes, and mostly compared with nights before treatment began.
how: Nine studies used wrist monitors or sleep-lab tests in children and teenagers with ADHD.
Nights on medicine were compared with nights without medicine.
The medicines were methylphenidate and amphetamine-type medicines.
In studies where children had taken the medicine for longer, the effect on the share of time in bed spent asleep looked smaller, but this does not prove sleep gets better.

cards.statement: Studies prove children's sleep gets better the longer they take ADHD stimulants like methylphenidate.

questions: Does melatonin help children on ADHD medicine fall asleep?

lines.short: Children on ADHD medicine fell asleep about 16 minutes sooner with melatonin than with a dummy pill.
lines.but: This was one small study of 19 children, paid for by the company that made the melatonin.
how: Each child took melatonin on some nights and a dummy pill on others, without knowing which.
Doctors did not see a bigger overall improvement with melatonin than with the dummy pill.
Reported health problems were mild or moderate, apart from one severe migraine, and about as common with the dummy pill.
All the children had first tried a bedtime routine that had not fixed their sleep.

questions: Is your thinking different the day after LSD?

lines.short: A few small changes, some better and some worse, which may just be chance.
lines.but: One study of 24 people after one small lab dose; this report gives no mood or sleep data.
how: People took LSD on one day and a dummy drink (placebo) on another, in random order.
The next morning, a few memory and word tests went a little better after LSD.
One card-sorting puzzle about switching rules went a little worse after LSD.
The researchers checked many scores without allowing for that, so some differences may be luck.

cards.statement: In a lab study, people's thinking was clearly worse the day after LSD.

questions: Can a bad reaction to PCP last for weeks?

lines.short: In three reported cases, a severe breakdown lasted two to four weeks, then passed.
lines.but: Only three cases from 1975, and nobody tested the drugs they had taken.
how: Three young men were treated in one hospital after street drugs thought to contain PCP.
They were confused, angry and unsteady, two heard voices, and one jumped from a high window.
All three got better, and afterwards remembered little of their illness.
Earlier studies the doctors cited said the mind effects of PCP usually last about a day.

cards.statement: A bad reaction to PCP always wears off within about a day.

questions: Does hospital medicine shorten a long breakdown after PCP?

lines.short: Nobody knows: in three cases, the medicines did not seem to shorten it.
